questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Discuss the composition and physical properties of the following parts of the Earth:

(i) Crust; (3 marks)

(ii) Mantle; (3 marks)

(iii) Core. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
All values are approximate, typical textbook figures.

**(i) The crust (3 marks).**

- The **outer, thin, rigid, solid and brittle layer**, separated from the mantle by the **Mohorovicic (Moho) discontinuity**.
- **Thickness:** **continental crust about 30 to 40 km (up to about 70 km under young mountain belts)**; **oceanic crust only about 5 to 10 km**.
- **Composition:** continental crust is **granitic (sial: silica and aluminium)**, with a more basic lower part; oceanic crust is **basaltic and gabbroic (sima: silica and magnesium)**. The most abundant elements are oxygen, silicon, aluminium, iron, calcium, sodium, potassium and magnesium.
- **Density:** about $2.7\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ (continental) and about $2.9$ to $3.0\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$ (oceanic). Temperature rises with depth at about $25$ to $30\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ per km. Seismic P-wave velocity about $6$ to $7\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$.

**(ii) The mantle (3 marks).**

- Lies between the Moho and the **core-mantle (Gutenberg) boundary at about 2900 km**; it makes up about 84 % of the Earth's volume.
- **Composition:** **ultrabasic silicate rock (peridotite)** rich in magnesium and iron, mainly olivine and pyroxene (with garnet), and denser high-pressure silicates in the lower mantle.
- **Physical properties:** density rising from about $3.3$ to about $5.5\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$; temperature from about $1000\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$ to over $3000\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$; it is **solid but flows very slowly (plastic)**, with a partly molten, weak layer, the **asthenosphere** (low velocity zone), under the rigid lithosphere. Seismic P-wave velocity increases from about $8$ to about $13.5\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$. Slow **convection currents** in the mantle move the plates.

**(iii) The core (3 marks).**

- From about **2900 km to the centre at 6371 km**.
- **Composition:** mainly **iron and nickel alloy**, with some lighter elements (sulphur, oxygen, silicon).
- **Physical properties:** the **outer core (to about 5150 km) is liquid** (S waves are not transmitted; it generates the Earth's magnetic field by movement of the liquid metal); the **inner core is solid** because of the very high pressure. Density about $10$ to $13\ \mathrm{g\,cm^{-3}}$; temperature about $4000$ to $6000\ ^\circ\mathrm{C}$; pressure about 3.6 million atmospheres at the centre.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Define the following terms:

(i) Earthquake magnitude; (2 marks)

(ii) Earthquake intensity. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Earthquake magnitude (2 marks).**

The **magnitude** is a measure of the **total energy released at the focus** of an earthquake, calculated from the amplitude of the waves recorded on a **seismograph** (corrected for the distance to the focus). It is a **single number** for the earthquake, given on the **logarithmic Richter scale** (or the moment magnitude scale): each increase of one unit means a tenfold increase in wave amplitude and about 32 times more energy.

**(ii) Earthquake intensity (2 marks).**

The **intensity** is a measure of the **effects (damage) of the earthquake at a given place** on people, buildings and the ground. It is described qualitatively on the **Mercalli scale** (modified Mercalli, I to XII). It is **different from place to place**, falling with distance from the epicentre, and depends also on the local ground and the type of buildings.

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) Name a body wave and outline its properties. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Body wave chosen: the P wave (primary, compressional or longitudinal wave).**

Properties:

1. **Particle motion is parallel to the direction of wave travel** (alternate compressions and dilations, like sound waves or a push-pull in a spring).
2. It is the **fastest seismic wave** (about $5$ to $7\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ in the crust and about $8\ \mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$ or more in the mantle), so it is the **first to arrive** on a seismogram.
3. It **travels through solids, liquids and gases**, so it passes through the liquid outer core, but it is **refracted (bent)** at the mantle-core boundary, which makes a **shadow zone** between about $104^\circ$ and $140^\circ$ from the focus.
4. It has a **smaller amplitude** and **causes less damage** than the surface waves.

(An S wave, which is slower, moves particles at right angles to the direction of travel and is not transmitted by liquids, would earn the same marks if its properties were given.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) (i) Define the term Environment. (3 marks)

(ii) State three ways by which flooding can be controlled. (3 marks)

(iii) Name two localities in Cameroon which are affected by occasional flooding. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Environment (3 marks).**

The **environment** is the **sum of all the external physical, chemical and biological conditions and influences** that surround and affect living organisms (including people) and the Earth's surface: the **land, water, air, rocks and soils, plants and animals**, and the human-made surroundings, which interact with each other.

**(ii) Three ways in which flooding can be controlled (3 marks).**

1. **Dams and reservoirs** on the river store the flood water and release it slowly.
2. **Artificial embankments (levees) and channel improvement** (deepening, widening, straightening and dredging the channel) increase the capacity of the channel; **diversion channels or spillways** take the excess water away.
3. **Afforestation and good land management in the catchment** (vegetation increases interception and infiltration and reduces run-off), together with **drainage, cleaning of gutters** and **land-use planning** (no buildings on flood plains) and flood warning.

**(iii) Two localities in Cameroon affected by occasional flooding (2 marks).**

- **Douala** (littoral region, low-lying and with many streams, mangrove and poor drainage).
- The **Logone flood plain in the Far North Region (for example around Yagoua and Kousseri)**, where the river overflows in the rainy season. (Other accepted examples: Limbe, Maroua.)
